newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends down, with focus on nearby spreads.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends down, with focus on nearby spreads.

text.p: Copper and aluminium ended near their lows on Friday after upside bids failed to catch fire in a thin market focused on next week's third Wednesday pricing.
Three-months copper finished the evening kerb on the London Metal Exchange (LME) at $2,132, off $26 from Thursday.
It started off on a weak note with a 7,225-tonne rise in LME stocks, but then made a halfhearted push towards $2,150 resistance during the midsession before drifting back.
"People basically want to square ahead of Christmas," a dealer said, adding that volumes were relatively thin.
Nearby spreads were the market's primary focus and remained tight. Heavy business was done in "tomorrow/next day" which traded close to the LME's $23 backwardation limit at $22.50.
"It's been a battle between the slightly higher than expected stocks pressuring prices and nearby tightness supporting the upside," said analyst Robin Bhar of brokers Brandeis.

Cash to threes backwardation continued to narrow, which is expected as third Wedneday pricing approaches and tight dates fall off the overall spread. It was last at around $100, down from $130 on Thursday.
But it was still wide enough to discourage a substantial sell-off, Bhar added.
Aluminium closely shadowed copper's movements, gaining strength early in the day from an LME stocks drawdown of 2,525 tonnes.
But producer forward selling capped the market and it failed to stay above the $1,540 resistance level for any length of time. It ended at its nearby support level of $1,510, down $18.
"Aluminium is still testing both sides of its trading range," Bhar said.
Lead was last bid at $696, down $4 from Thursday's bullish close at the psychological $700 level.
But analysts said it was still looking constructive following Thursday's run-up to two-week highs, which was attributed to options-related and Far East buying.
"There are strong hints lead has seen its lows," analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said in a commentary.
Nickel shed $70 to finish at $6,635, under pressure from a sizable 876-tonne increase in stocks.
Analysts noted it was creeping closer to its technical objective of $6,660 and remained vulnerable to the downside.
Zinc ended the kerb slightly weaker at $1,053, down $5, while tin was down $55 at $5,775.
Alloy was last bid just $1 higher at $1,363 after.
